ops.text: 5.5 Proprietary Rights. As between the Parties, the Company owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to (i) the Content, the Marks and all other materials furnished by the Company under this Agreement, and (ii) all customer, user, order and transaction data collected through or generated by the Site in connection with Deerskin Products (the "Company Data"). HDI hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest in and to the design, look and feel, and other materials and work product developed specifically for the Company or the Site under this Agreement (the "Deliverables"), excluding HDI's pre-existing and generally applicable software, systems, tools and know-how, which HDI retains and in respect of which HDI grants the Company a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the same to the extent embedded in or reasonably necessary to use the Deliverables. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to HDI any right, title or interest in the Content, the Marks, the Company Data or any other Company intellectual property, and no joint ownership of any of the foregoing is created.

quote: 2.1 The Company shall provide all Content to HDI to be included in the Site no later than ten (10) days from the date this Agreement has been executed by both Parties.
rationale: The Agreement contains no ownership or intellectual property provision anywhere: it addresses Content delivery (2.1), editorial control (5.2), a limited licence of the Company's Marks to HDI (6.1) and customer e-mail list cross-promotion (7.1), but never states who owns the Site deliverables HDI develops, the Content the Company supplies, or the customer, user and order data generated by the Site. With no clause at all, the rule's preferred and fallback positions are both unmet and the Company's Content, Marks and Site data are left unprotected (and could be claimed by HDI as developer/host). We have inserted a Proprietary Rights section (5.5) confirming Company ownership of Content, Marks and Company Data, assignment of the Site Deliverables to the Company with HDI retaining its pre-existing platform and tools under a perpetual, royalty-free licence back to us, and expressly excluding any assignment of Company IP/data to HDI and any joint ownership. Because HDI bears the development costs, the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Deliverables in lieu of assignment) is offered in the comment as an acceptable landing zone.

quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products
rationale: Section 6.1 binds the Company (our party) to exclusivity for the whole term. The term under Section 4.1 is one year but renews automatically each anniversary indefinitely, and the only exit (90 days' notice) triggers a Termination Payment under Section 4.2(a), so the covenant effectively runs for the full, open-ended term with no performance-based release. proposal.summary: Add an express Customer convenience termination right on 90 days' notice and cap the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3.1 payments.

quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
rationale: Section 4.1 only lets either Party stop the annual auto-renewal on ninety (90) days' written notice, so the Company has no mid-term convenience right, and Section 4.2(a) imposes a Termination Payment of 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 (payable in eight quarterly instalments) on any Company termination. That is an uncapped exit penalty running to many multiples of three months' Section 3.1 fees (30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per month), so the clause fails the fallback on a material term. We take the fallback: an express Customer convenience right on 90 days' written notice, with the Termination Payment capped at the payments made to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date. HDI's convenience right already sits at the fallback, being exercisable only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

verification.notes: All fallback elements are satisfied: an express Customer convenience right at 90 days' notice (within the 60–90 day band), an early-termination fee capped at three months' Section 3.1 payments, and HDI's convenience right confined by the pre-existing renewal mechanic to term end on 90 days' notice. Preferred is not met: notice is 90 rather than 30 days and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, only a (now capped) Termination Payment. Consistent with the locked fallback target. The two edits are narrow — one inserted sentence and one proviso appended to the existing formula; the rest of Section 4.1, including the Net Sales formula and the eight quarterly instalment mechanic, remains effective. The bracketed gloss "for purposes of this Section 4.1, 'Customer' means the Company" is arguably avoidable (the sentence could have named the Company directly), but it cures an otherwise undefined term and introduces no contradiction, so minimality and intent are preserved. Margin comment accurately describes the operative changes and cites the playbook cap.
